detail_text: Specifically, In WX-SOP-10217: Laboratory Investigation Report Procedure, Section 5.5.9.1, states: "If no root cause is identified through phase 1 and 2 investigations, upon consultation with QA, the investigation may progress to retesting.". Section 5.5.9.5 specifies: "If all results meet specification, are within system suitability and sample acceptance criteria the re-testing can be reported and the original analysis invalidated.". This SOP allows retesting and subsequently invalidate the original results if no root cause has been identified, which is inappropriate. When no clear laboratory error has been identified, the initial results may constitute valid analytical findings that should be reported and considered in the batch release decisions. SEE

detail_text: Specifically, You have not implemented your documented risk management procedure, Quality Risk Assessment Process SOP MDSPS-B-186 Rev 1 dated 10/21/2024, in the following areas: A. Regulatory Compliance Risk Assessment: The firm failed to conduct risk assessments prior to product distribution to ensure regulatory compliance requirements are met. Products continue to be distributed without appropriate premarket authorization, indicating inadequate risk evaluation of regulatory compliance impacts. B. Product Risk Management Documentation: Risk management documentation is madequate for individual device types, with a single FMEA table applied across all lubricant devices rather than device-specific risk analyses. Risk identification is mcomplete, failing to systematically address environmental, biological, functional, and mechanical hazards as required for comprehensive risk Surveillance Risk Assessment: The complaint handling system lacks risk-based prioritization, treating all complaints with equal severity regardless of potential safety impact. Data aggregation and trend analysis are not performed to identify emerging risks from post-market feedback. D. Supplier and Material Change Risk Assessment: Changes to preservative raw material specifications and suppliers [redacted] were implemented without conducting risk assessments to evaluate potential impacts on device safety and performance. The change control process does not incorporate systematic risk evaluation as required E. Design Change Risk Assessment: Modifications to package size and cap configuration were implemented without risk assessment to determine potential impacts on product safety and effectiveness. Design change controls lack integration with risk management processes. F. Manufacturing Process Change Risk Assessment: Changes to manufacturing batch sizes were implemented without risk-based evaluation of potential impacts on product quality and safety. Process validation gaps in packaging and sealing operations were not identified through risk assessment, resulting in quality issues including leakage and potential contamination risks. This systemic failure to apply risk-based thinking throughout the quality management system demonstrates non-conformance.

For example, your firm uses contracted laboratories that are not registered or inspected by the agency to perform incoming raw material and finished OTC drug product testing, including the Certificate of Analysis (CoA) used to support the release decision. In addition, no Quality Agreements have been established between your firm and the contracted laboratories to define roles, responsibilities, and oversight related to testing, data integrity, and compliance with cGMP requirements. Moreover, no documented evidence was provided, which demonstrates that the selected contracted laboratories have been inspected by your Quality Unit to assess their compliance with applicable cGMP requirements. SEE B. A quality agreement has not been established between your firm and the owner of the U.S.- marketed me OTC product. As a result, there is no assurance that effective quality systems and controls are consistently implemented, as the roles and responsibilities ofeach party involved in contract manufacturing, packaging, testing, release, and post-distribution quality activities are not clearly defined. These deficiencies may adversely affect your firm’s ability to adequately oversee cGMP activities and to promptly identify, investigate, and address potential quality issues affecting products distributed to the U.S. market. C. Your firm was unable to provide the corrective and preventive action (CAPA) reports generated by your Quality Unit in response to the seventeen (17) objectionable conditions documented in the FDA Form 483 issued during the previous inspection on July 2, 2020.
